main_body: Tall Parisian-style townhouse: slate mansard roof with two dormers and a chimney, a brick facade with four lit windows per floor, a balcony, and a striped-awning shopfront.
top_band: Rows 17-22, L~95-122, a grey-blue band that stays in the same lightness family as the slate below it (L 79-103). It reads as a roof parapet seen face-on, not a horizontal top surface.
evidence: The scan at x=16, 32 and 47 shows no step of 25 L or more between a top surface and the roof face. Row 17 (L122), rows 18-22 (L95), a single edge row 23 (L122) and a dark row 24 (L53) lead straight into slate rows of L79-103. The roof is drawn as a vertical mansard facade with dormers painted flat on it, and no horizontal roof top is visible from above. Below it the brick wall, windows, balcony, awning and shopfront are all vertical faces drawn straight on, like an architectural elevation. Compared with the references, whose roofs are large sloped planes with hips and gables, the top here is missing.

style.evidence: The brick, slate and window glow have decent ramps and dots, and the 14 colours per tile is within the reference range (11-18). Flat-fill coverage is only 2%. However, 91% of the dark edge pixels are neutral, against 7-9% for both references, so the outline reads as a near-black sticker line rather than the dark tone of the neighbouring material. Total distinct colours (56) are far below house-h101_0 (185) and below house-h112_0-stone (66). The result is thinner and more sticker-like than the references.
